prompt: Which question does a smoke test answer?
hint: It comes before every other test on a build.

choices.text: Does the fix Rui just made work?
choices.why: That is one change checked in depth: sanity, lesson 9.

choices.text: Is this build worth testing at all?
choices.why: Right: a gate before the testing, not a search for defects.

choices.text: Did the change break something that used to work?
choices.why: That is regression, lesson 10, broad and deep.

choices.text: Does the product meet R1 to R9?
choices.why: That takes every case; smoke touches each area once.

prompt: Match each kind of testing to its shape.
hint: One description is no kind of testing the lesson names.

pairs.right: Wide and shallow, first on every build
Narrow and deep, on one change
Broad and deep, rerunning what passed

right_distractors: Clicking around until something looks wrong

prompt: Why does a smoke test have to be quick?
hint: When is it most needed?

choices.text: Quick tests find more defects per minute
choices.why: Smoke is not looking for defects in detail at all.

choices.text: The developer is blocked until it finishes
choices.why: The developer goes on working; it is the tester who waits on the result.

choices.text: A slow one gets skipped on the day it matters
choices.why: Right: the third build of a bad afternoon is exactly when it matters.

choices.text: It has to be automated, and automation is fast
choices.why: It can be run by hand in a couple of minutes.

prompt: A build arrives in which booking crashes, and nobody runs smoke. What does it cost, as the lesson tells it?
hint: Ana starts on risk A.

choices.text: Nothing: the first discount case finds it just as fast
choices.why: It finds a failure, and the next two do too, before the pattern shows.

choices.text: One fault becomes several failed cases and reports
choices.why: Right: three reports for Rui to close as duplicates, and a lost hour.

choices.text: The defect reaches the theatre, because cases do not cover booking
choices.why: The cases do cover it; they just spend an hour on a broken build first.

choices.text: The plan has to be rewritten for the new build
choices.why: The plan already says what to do; nobody checked it.

prompt: A smoke run's result is a ___, not a score: all pass and testing starts, one fails and it waits.
hint: Something you go through or not.

prompt: Why does boxoffice's booking check book Hamlet rather than The Seagull?
hint: When does The Seagull stop selling?

choices.text: Hamlet costs more, so a wrong price would show
choices.why: Prices are cases; smoke does not check the total.

choices.text: Hamlet has fewer seats, so overselling would show sooner
choices.why: Two tickets out of 80 shows nothing about overselling.

choices.text: The Seagull closes at 19:00, so its check would fail every evening
choices.why: Right: a check has to answer the same whatever the time.

choices.text: The Seagull is the first row, which the home page check reads
choices.why: Checks are independent; reading a row does not book it.

prompt: Which of these does a good smoke check need? Choose every one the lesson lists.
hint: Five conditions; two of these are not among them.

choices.text: It follows an area's main path with ordinary data
choices.why: Shallow: nothing unusual.

choices.text: Its expected result can be seen at a glance
choices.why: A title, a line, a number, decided in advance.

choices.text: It covers every discount rule in one request
choices.why: That is a decision table's work, lesson 5.

choices.text: It gives the same answer whatever the day and time
choices.why: Otherwise it fails for reasons that are not the build.

choices.text: It uses the order the previous check created
choices.why: Checks depend on nothing but the server being up.

choices.text: It touches one major area
choices.why: So that the list as a whole covers them all.

prompt: Which of these belongs in the test cases rather than the smoke list?
hint: Does it need arithmetic or judgement to read?

choices.text: /health answers "ok boxoffice" with the version number
choices.why: It is the plan's entry criterion, the first smoke check.

choices.text: A member booking five tickets gets 15% off
choices.why: Right: a discount rule with arithmetic, one of many cases in lesson 5.

choices.text: The home page lists the three shows
choices.why: The catalogue loads: a smoke check.

choices.text: The outbox opens
choices.why: The test build's mail stop answers: a smoke check.

prompt: boxoffice gains a page of audience reviews for each show. How do you decide whether it gets a smoke check?
hint: Imagine that page dead.

choices.text: Every new page gets one, so that coverage stays complete
choices.why: That grows smoke into regression; coverage is the cases' job.

choices.text: Ask if the build is still worth testing with it dead
choices.why: Right: if yes, no smoke check; if no, it gets one.

choices.text: Add one if the reviews feature carries a high risk
choices.why: Risk decides how deeply cases test it, not whether it gates the build.

choices.text: Leave it out until it has a defect
choices.why: A smoke check exists before the failure, not after it.

prompt: In smoke.sh, what does ${form:+-d "$form"} do?
hint: Four of the five checks have an empty form.

choices.text: Sends an empty form with every request
choices.why: With an empty field it adds nothing at all.

choices.text: Adds -d and the form only when there is one
choices.why: Right: one loop sends plain requests and the booking.

choices.text: Sends the form to /book whatever the path says
choices.why: The path comes from its own field; nothing here names /book.

choices.text: Hides curl's error messages when a check fails
choices.why: That is -s, earlier on the same line.

prompt: Hamlet starts with 80 seats. After one smoke run on a fresh start, how many does the home page show left?
hint: The booking check takes two.

prompt: Why restart boxoffice after a smoke run and before the cases?
hint: What did the booking check leave?

choices.text: Smoke slows the server down until it restarts
choices.why: Nothing in the lesson points at speed.

choices.text: The outbox fills up with smoke e-mails
choices.why: The smoke list sends no e-mail; it only opens the outbox.

choices.text: A passing run locks the application against changes
choices.why: There is no such lock in boxoffice.

choices.text: An order and two seats are gone
choices.why: Right: 78 seats and order 1002 next would throw the cases off.

prompt: Why does smoke.sh end with [ "$failed" -eq 0 ]?
hint: echo $? prints what it leaves behind.

choices.text: So the exit status says whether any check failed
choices.why: Right: another program, or &&, can tell without reading the lines.

choices.text: To print how many checks failed
choices.why: The echo on the line above prints the count.

choices.text: To run the failed checks a second time
choices.why: It runs nothing; it only compares a number.

choices.text: To stop boxoffice when a check fails
choices.why: The script never touches the server process.

prompt: All five checks fail, the first one included. What is the likeliest reading?
hint: What does the first check ask?

choices.text: Five defects, one per area, each needing its own report
choices.why: They share a cause: four fail because the first did.

choices.text: Nothing is answering; the rest follow from it
choices.why: Right: one request to /health confirms it.

choices.text: The smoke script has a mistake in it
choices.why: The same script passed on the last build; test the server first.

choices.text: The data has run out, since every seat was booked
choices.why: Two seats per run, against hundreds, and /health has no data.

prompt: Smoke has failed on a new build. Put what Ana does in order.
hint: Her own side first.
items: Tell Rui once, with the smoke output
Run smoke on the next build
Restart and resume the blocked cases
trap: Telling Rui before ruling out the lab sends him after her own Ctrl-C.

prompt: Only the booking check fails; the other four pass. What does the plan's suspension criterion suggest?
hint: Which cases run through booking?

choices.text: Nothing stops: four of five passed
choices.why: The one that failed is the area most cases need.

choices.text: Everything stops, sign-up included
choices.why: Sign-up cases that never book do not depend on it.

choices.text: Booking and what needs it stop; the rest goes on
choices.why: Right: discounts and orders wait, and the plan records the call.

choices.text: Report it, and start the discount cases anyway, since they come first
choices.why: Every discount case books first, so each would fail at step one.

prompt: The booking check failed, and on a second run, with nothing changed, it passes. What is that?
hint: Would a customer get the same answer twice?

choices.text: Proof that the first failure was the lab
choices.why: Nothing in the lab changed between the runs.

choices.text: Good news: testing resumes, and there is nothing to note
choices.why: A failure nobody can explain does not go away by passing once.

choices.text: A finding of its own: an intermittent failure
choices.why: Right: intermittent is still a failure, and Rui needs to know.

choices.text: A mistake in smoke.sh, to fix before the next build
choices.why: The script sends the same request each time; look at the build first.

prompt: A web shop has search, a basket, payment and accounts. Which is a good smoke check for it?
hint: Main path, ordinary data, seconds.

choices.text: Search with two hundred misspellings of product names
choices.why: Many values with judgement about each: a case design job.

choices.text: Search for a product that exists and see it listed
choices.why: Right: one area, its main path, a result seen at a glance.

choices.text: Pay with each of the six card brands the shop accepts
choices.why: Six checks of one area, and paying for real is not shallow.

choices.text: Check that every product image has a text alternative
choices.why: Worth doing, as accessibility cases; a missing one leaves the build testable.

prompt: A team's smoke check books tonight's show, and it fails every run after 21:00. What is wrong?
hint: Section 03's fifth condition.

choices.text: The check depends on the time of day
choices.why: Right: it should book a show that can be booked at any hour.

choices.text: Every evening build is broken, so testing should move to mornings
choices.why: The builds may be fine; the check fails for its own reason.

choices.text: The server cannot handle evening traffic
choices.why: Smoke sends five requests; there is no traffic to speak of.

choices.text: Booking closing is a defect to report every evening
choices.why: Closing before the show is what the requirement asks for.

prompt: Suspension has an other half, the criterion for starting again: the ___ criterion.
hint: In boxoffice's case, a new build that passes smoke.
